free_tier.stated: 1 dedicated gateway included on Free; serves only CIDs pinned to your own account unless a Gateway Access Control is added. 10 GB/month bandwidth, 10,000 requests/month on Free.

egress.terms: Metered at 10 GB/month and 10,000 requests/month on Free. '10GB of Bandwidth per month through Dedicated Gateway / 10,000 Requests per month through Dedicated Gateway' (free-plan announcement). Unmetered request rate, but hard monthly byte cap.

tooling: Any HTTP client against <name>.mypinata.cloud; Pinata SDK gateways.public.get(); custom domain available on paid plans only.
chaining: 1 GB storage per account is the ceiling, so a dedicated gateway can only ever front 1 GB of content per free account. Chaining accounts does not help because a dedicated gateway is restricted to its own account's pins by default — you would need a Gateway Access Control per gateway to serve cross-account CIDs, which is a paid/enterprise feature.
limits_note: Restricted-by-default gateway; Custom Domain required to serve HTML; 10 GB/mo bandwidth; 10k req/mo.
reliability_note: The architectural point that kills this class: a *dedicated* gateway is account-scoped, so it cannot be used as a shared egress tier for other people's content, and a *shared* gateway (gateway.pinata.cloud) is unmetered but serves only public IPFS content — you still need somewhere to pin 500 GB, which Free does not provide.

evidence.proved: 'All Pinata Dedicated Gateways are restricted by default. This mean they will only serve CIDs that are pinned to your account'
